newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algiers puts main areas off limits to vehicles.
newsitem.headline: Algiers puts main areas off limits to vehicles.

text.p: Algeria announced on Sunday details of a draconian ban on vehicles stopping in main streets and squares in the capital to try to thwart car bomb attacks, which the authorities blame on Moslem fundamentalists.

From Wednesday, all vehicles are banned from stopping between 7 a.m. and 7 p.m. in 37 main roads and seven squares, including Colonel Amirouche Boulevard where a car bomb killed more than 40 people and wounded 300 in January 1995.
It also announced that attendants at municipal vehicle parks would be appointed, after investigation by security forces, and would have powers to control and search vehicles.

Parking will also be banned outside markets, schools, the parliament building, mosques, court offices, main post office and 'house of the press', a complex of newspaper offices, said the official Algerian news agency APS.
Car bombs have killed scores of people in Algiers and other towns, including several outside markets and one outside the newspaper complex.

Traders and residents in the affected areas can get exceptional authority for vehicles to stop between 9 a.m. and 11 a.m. to load or unload. Fees for municipal vehicle parks will be reduced by 25 percent.
APS quoted Cherif Rahmani, minister responsible for Algiers, as saying the measures were being taken for "security, civic and environmental motives".
"It is opportune today to return priority to pedestrians and collective transport to the detriment of the individual vehicle," he said.
